narrative.title: Cataloguing the Repeated Yard Layouts
narrative.scenario: A city planner scans a zoning map where built lots (1) form clusters separated by empty land (0). Two clusters built on the same footprint — same relative shape, regardless of where they sit on the map — count as one design. The planning office needs the number of distinct designs present, rotations and reflections counting as different designs.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x m binary grid where 1 marks a built lot and 0 empty land.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of distinct island shapes, where two islands are identical only if one translates exactly onto the other.

testCases.explanation: Both clusters are the same 2x1 domino footprint, one row apart.
An L-shaped cluster and a single-lot cluster are two different designs.

hintLevels: Level 1: Shape, not position, is the identity — translate every island to a common origin before comparing.
Level 2: During DFS collect each cell's offset from the island's first cell; the sorted offset set is the signature.
Level 3: Drop the signatures into a set and return its size — hashing does the dedup for free.
